chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm narrated from his father, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, from Zurārah, who said:

Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام attended the funeral of a man from Quraysh, and I was with him. ʿAṭāʾ was also present there. Then a wailing woman cried out, so ʿAṭāʾ said: “She must surely become silent, or else we shall surely return.” He said: But she did not become silent, so ʿAṭāʾ went back.

He said: So I said to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, “ʿAṭāʾ has gone back.” He said, “And why?” I said, “This crying woman cried out, and he said to her: ‘She must surely become silent, or else we shall surely return,’ but she did not become silent, so he went back.” He said: “Proceed with us; for if, whenever we saw something false alongside the truth, we were to abandon the truth because of it, we would not fulfill the right of a Muslim.”

He said: When he had performed salat over the funeral, its guardian said to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, “Return, rewarded—may Allah have mercy on you—for you are not able to walk.” But he refused to return. He said: So I said to him, “He has given you permission to return, and I have a need about which I want to ask you.” So he said: “Carry on, for we did not come by his permission, nor do we return by his permission. Rather, it is only virtue and reward that we sought, and according to how far a man follows the funeral, he is rewarded for that.”

key_terms.الْبَاطِلِ: that which is false or wrongful
key_terms.الْحَقِّ: that which is rightfully due or true
key_terms.جَنَازَةَ: funeral procession or bier of the deceased
key_terms.حَقَّ مُسْلِمٍ: the due right owed to a Muslim
key_terms.صَارِخَةٌ: a woman crying out loudly in lamentation
key_terms.وَلِيُّهَا: the guardian or responsible relative of the deceased

ai.seo_question: Should a person leave a funeral procession if some wrongful behavior occurs during it?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates that Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام continued accompanying a funeral despite the presence of objectionable wailing, teaching that a false element accompanying a rightful act does not nullify the duty owed to a Muslim. It also shows that accompanying a جنازة and continuing with it is a meritorious act for which reward is given in proportion to one’s participation.
